articles.title: HOW TO DEBUG WITH LOGS, TRACES, AND ERRORS TOGETHER: SENTRY WORKSHOP
articles.summary:
Most devs use logs as part of their debugging toolkit, but few get the most out of them. In this live workshop, “Sentry Logs, Beyond the Basics [5],” you'll learn how to:

* Debug with logs, traces, and errors to get to a root cause faster * Keep context intact [6] by logging across service boundaries as a request crosses processes and languages * Tune signal to noise by determining which log levels actually matter and how to sample without losing the one log you needed

articles.title: HOW WE MADE CLAUDE.AI 3X FASTER IN TWO WEEKS
articles.summary: Anthropic made the core Claude web and desktop experience about three times faster during a two-week sprint, cutting the 75th-percentile fresh-load time from 3.1 seconds to 0.55 seconds. The team used Claude to create deterministic benchmarks, pursue bottlenecks in parallel, and lock in gains with CI ratchets, feature flags, and staged rollouts.

articles.title: RENDERING HUGE PULL REQUESTS IN THE GITHUB COPILOT APP
articles.summary: GitHub rebuilt the Copilot app's pull request view to keep a diff with 2,200 files, more than one million changed lines, and over 400 inline comments responsive. The design separates fixed code geometry from lazily measured comment blocks, then uses permanent instrumentation and automated stress loops to catch scroll jumps, leaks, and jank.

articles.title: WHY WEBSOCKETS BEAT SSE FOR AI STREAMING AT SCALE
articles.summary: WebSockets provide the bidirectional channel that agentic interfaces need for cancellation, approvals, and steering while a response is still streaming. They also reduce per-message overhead and support ordered binary data, but teams must still add reconnection, delivery guarantees, fan-out, and operational tooling themselves.

articles.title: WE ARE ALL PRODUCT ENGINEERS NOW
articles.summary: As code generation gets cheaper, software work shifts toward discovering what customers need, defining what good looks like, and making products delightful. The forecast assumes agents will absorb more of review, maintenance, deployment, and scaling, which makes product judgment and tacit knowledge more valuable than routine implementation.

articles.title: AGENTIC CODING: BET ON THE PRIMITIVES
articles.summary: AI coding agents lower the cost of building thin, team-owned layers on top of focused primitives, changing when it makes sense to install a framework. Mature libraries still win for commodity UI and accessibility-heavy components, because agents reduce implementation effort without replacing domain knowledge.

articles.title: GEMINI 3.8 TEXT-TO-SPEECH SAYS HELLO
articles.summary: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS adds prompt-designed and replicated voices with line-by-line control over pacing, emotion, accents, and dialogue across more than 100 languages and dialects. Flash-Lite targets high-volume use, while consent verification, SynthID watermarking, and C2PA credentials add safeguards for generated audio.

articles.title: TINYJS
articles.summary: TinyJS packages cross-platform desktop apps at roughly 6 MB by pairing a JavaScript backend with each operating system's native webview instead of bundling Chromium. It includes system APIs, hot reload, signed builds, and socket-based page-to-backend RPC, with Windows and Linux still marked beta.

articles.title: ELECTROBUN 2.0
articles.summary: Electrobun 2.0 builds cross-platform desktop apps with a native main process, system webviews by default, and optional bundled Chromium or WGPU surfaces. Its new Hutch toolchain, Cottontail TypeScript runtime, multi-language main processes, differential updates, signing, and templates aim to keep releases small, with a basic app around 1.28 MiB.

articles.title: SELF-IMPROVING AGENT HARNESSES OVERFIT. HOW GOOGLE FIXES IT
articles.summary: Self-improving harnesses can memorize the evaluation set they evolve against, producing large in-distribution gains that mostly disappear on unseen tasks. Google's RRSI regularizes harness edits with sparsity and magnitude penalties plus noise-aware acceptance rules, improving the held-out average from 39.7 to 43.6 while using 36% fewer tokens than unregularized evolution.

articles.title: BUILDING TOOLS FOR AI AGENTS
articles.summary: Reliable agent tools must separate a user's identity from delegated authority, return clear operation states, and distinguish permission failures from temporary service errors. The article also recommends safe retry contracts, idempotency support, and repeatable evaluations that test task completion, recovery behavior, cost, and unauthorized actions.

articles.title: THE COMPLETE GUIDE TO CLOUDFLARE QUICK TUNNELS
articles.summary: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels expose a local server at a temporary HTTPS URL with one cloudflared command, without requiring an account, DNS changes, or an open router port. They work well for webhooks, mobile testing, demos, coding-agent previews, POST streaming, and WebSockets, but use a random hostname that disappears when the process stops. The tradeoffs include a 200-request concurrency limit, no SLA, no Cloudflare Access, and buffered SSE, so persistent or production workflows should move to a named tunnel.

articles.title: REDIS WAS BUILT FOR SINGLE-CORE MACHINES. YOURS HAS 64
UNIVER
articles.summary: Univer is an open-source, plugin-based Office SDK for embedding spreadsheets, documents, presentations, and headless agent workflows in browser and Node.js applications.

articles.title: HOW NOTION HANDLES CONCURRENT EDITING WITH CRDTS
articles.summary: Notion replaced last-write-wins block text with an RGA-based CRDT so concurrent and offline edits can merge without silently discarding changes.

articles.title: SHOW KEYSTROKES ON A WEBSITE WITH THE SHOW-KEYSTROKES CUSTOM ELEMENT
articles.summary: The show-keystrokes web component displays keyboard input inside the page, making shortcuts visible in tab or window screen shares without a separate desktop utility.

articles.title: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE MODEL EATS THE STACK?
articles.summary: Stronger general coding agents will absorb much task-specific data-agent scaffolding, leaving persistent semantic context, consistency, storage, and compression as the more durable systems problems.
